meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_146_packages.json, and the full source text torah_146.txt. Verified that torahData.js contains ZERO edges with reference===146. All concepts in this analysis are sourced from the text itself. For each statement in the source text, bechina markers were checked: בְּחִינַת, הַנִּקְרֵאת, זֶה בְּחִינַת, הָיָה בּוֹ (in equating sense), and related equivalence language. Each concept was checked against the full dataset (cross-reference search) to determine if its node_id already appears in torahData.js for other references, and proposed as a gap addition if it constitutes a genuine bechina node rather than a descriptive or eitza element. Since reference 146 has zero dataset coverage, ALL 10 proposed nodes are gaps.

The text establishes three bechina-faces of Torah in this Torah: (a) Torah IS CALLED (הַנִּקְרֵאת) a woman (אִשָּׁה) — this is the opening paradox; (b) Torah IS the one that 'makes the simple wise' (מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי) — cited from Psalm 19:8 as Torah's defining quality; (c) Torah IS the one standing in the secret place calling out 'mi peti yasur hena' — she IS present where men are not accustomed to be. additions.reason: The verse cited — 'עֵדוּת ה' נֶאֱמָנָה מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי' (Psalm 19:8) — defines Torah as 'the testimony of God' (עֵדוּת ה'). The teaching's whole argument turns on the fact that Torah IS testimony (עֵדוּת) — it IS the faithful witness to what happens in the hidden domain of sin. The identity Torah = עֵדוּת is the foundational bechina of the entire teaching: Torah is the one who SEES what happens in the secret, and therefore can TESTIFY. The text closes with this: 'בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה הַתּוֹרָה... יְכוֹלָה לְהָעִיד' — Torah can bear witness (עֵדוּת) precisely because of her identity as the one standing where others don't go. עֵדוּת IS Torah's identity in this teaching.

additions.reason: The phrase 'מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי' (making the simple wise) serves a double function in this teaching: (1) it IS a bechina of Torah — the verse says Torah IS 'עֵדוּת ה' נֶאֱמָנָה מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי', meaning making-the-simple-wise IS what Torah essentially is in this context; and (2) it IS the bechina of חֲרָטָה (regret) — the text explicitly states 'הַחֲרָטָה, זֶה בְּחִינַת מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי'. This dual role — Torah's quality AND the essential equivalent of regret — makes מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי the pivotal concept of Package 1. It is the bridge between Torah's nature and the human experience of post-sin wisdom. Its degree (3 connections) reflects these two explicit bechina links: to Torah and to חֲרָטָה, plus the implicit link to the concept of פֶּתִי as recipient.

Note that חֲרָטָה IS the first stage of teshuva and represents the turning from the evil pole (Package 2) toward the good pole (Package 1).

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_note: Torah #146 follows the classic good/evil mirror structure perfectly. The evil pole (Package 2: תַּאֲווֹת, מַיִם גְּנוּבִים, הַסֵּתֶר, רוּחַ שְׁטוּת, עֲבֵרָה) is the domain where the sinner lives at the moment of sin. The good pole (Package 1: תּוֹרָה, אִשָּׁה, עֵדוּת, מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי, חֲרָטָה) is the domain of Torah's redemptive power that reaches into the evil domain. The eitza arc between them: [Pkg 2: evil lust in secret] → [BRIDGE: Torah stands in that secret place] → [Pkg 1: Torah's testimony and wisdom-making draw forth regret]. The point of fracture — the concept that can tip either way — is הַסֵּתֶר (the hidden domain): it is where evil operates, but also where Torah stands as witness.
analysis_notes.structural_note: Torah #146 is one of the shortest teachings in LM Volume 1: 5 sentences, 0 dataset edges. Despite its brevity, it is conceptually dense: the entire teaching rests on a paradox (woman testifying) resolved by a structural insight (Torah as witness in the hidden domain of lust). The teaching has a complete good/evil binary structure with a clear eitza flow from evil to good through the mechanism of post-sin regret.
